chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Wahb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who severs ties with his relatives who do not recognize the Truth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not befitting for him to sever ties with them.'
ai.seo_question: Should one cut off family ties if they are disbelievers or do not recognize the truth?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that severing kinship ties (qat' al-rahim) is not befitting even with relatives who are ignorant of the Truth (ahl al-batil), emphasizing that kinship obligations transcend doctrinal disagreement. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on maintaining social bonds and family unity as a distinct virtue, separate from the political or theological stance one takes toward those relatives. It serves as a practical guideline for believers to preserve familial harmony without necessarily compromising their religious identity.
